name: Berkshire
description: Berkshire is a prosperous county west of London, combining attractive countryside with major towns and business centres. It is particularly known for Windsor, the Thames Valley, historic estates and technology companies around Reading and Maidenhead.

places.name: Bracknell Forest
places.description: A district in Berkshire built up substantially as a post-war New Town, with the ancient Windsor Great Park and Swinley Forest woodland nearby.

places.name: Windsor and Maidenhead
places.description: A district in Berkshire home to Windsor Castle, the oldest and largest inhabited castle in the world and a working royal residence.

places.name: Slough
places.description: A large town in Berkshire that grew rapidly as an industrial estate hub from the 1920s, now a diverse, fast-growing commercial centre near Heathrow.

places.name: Reading
places.description: A large town in Berkshire on the Thames and Kennet rivers, known for its major music festival, tech industry presence, and historic abbey ruins.

places.name: West Berkshire
places.description: A large rural district in Berkshire covering the market town of Newbury, known for its racecourse and the rolling North Wessex Downs.

places.name: Wokingham
places.description: An affluent commuter town in Berkshire, historically a centre for silk weaving, now known for its Georgian high street and leafy surrounding countryside.
